cards.text: The scribes and chief priests know Jesus just told a parable against them, and they want Him arrested, but they're afraid of the people. So they watch Him closely and send spies who pretend to be sincere. Friend, that's the car warranty call that's “just checking in on you.”

cards.question: The spies are only pretending to be sincere. What are they really hoping to do?
If the spies can catch Jesus, the plan is to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the ___.

cards.text: The spies walk up all smiles: “Teacher,” they say, “we know that You speak and teach correctly.” Friend, that's the coworker who tells you you're AMAZING at spreadsheets right before he hands you his.

cards.question: After all that flattery, what question do the spies ask Jesus?

answers.text: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar
Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath
Is it lawful to divorce a wife

cards.question: Jesus falls for the spies' act.

cards.text: Jesus sees right through them and says, “Show Me a denarius.” Me, friend? One compliment about my mustache and I'm already packing you a cookie box.

cards.question: Jesus asks whose image and inscription are on the denarius. The spies answer that they belong to ___.
Caesar's face is on the coin the spies are holding. So what does Jesus tell them?

answers.text: Give Caesar what is his and God what is His
Give Caesar nothing and give God everything
Give God first and Caesar what is left over

cards.text: And all of this is happening right in front of the people. Friend, that's the whole office leaning in when the boss says, “Can I see you a minute?”

cards.question: The spies manage to trap Jesus in His words in front of the people.
The spies are ___ at Jesus' answer, and they fall ___.

cards.text: Then some Sadducees, a group of Jewish leaders, come to question Jesus. Friend, that's round two. DING DING.

cards.question: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.

cards.text: They open with something Moses, Israel's leader, wrote about a man whose brother dies and leaves a wife but no children. Oh, they came with the RULEBOOK, friend.

cards.question: According to what Moses wrote, what is the living brother supposed to do?

answers.text: Marry the widow and raise children for his brother
Look after the widow until she marries again
Give the widow his brother's land and house

cards.text: Now their story: SEVEN brothers, and the first one marries a wife but dies childless. Friend, when a story starts with seven brothers, clear your whole afternoon.

cards.question: Then the second brother and the third marry the widow. How does it go for all seven brothers?

answers.text: All seven die and leave no children
The seventh brother finally has a son
The last brother refuses to marry her

cards.text: And last of all, the woman dies. Friend, I've heard shorter setups from a man asking to borrow twenty dollars.

cards.question: Here's the Sadducees' big question: in the resurrection, whose ___ will she be?

cards.text: Jesus answers, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.” Notice that word, friend. THIS age.

cards.question: Jesus says those worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection will still marry.
Jesus says those in the resurrection can no longer die. Why?

answers.text: Because they are like the angels
Because they never sinned on earth
Because they live far from the earth

cards.text: Since they are sons of the resurrection, Jesus says, they are sons of God. Then He says even Moses shows that the dead are raised, the SAME Moses the Sadducees just quoted, and friend, that's getting your own screenshot sent right back to you.

cards.question: To show it, Jesus points to the passage about the burning ___.

cards.text: There Moses calls the Lord “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” Friend, those three forefathers of Israel had all died, and the Lord is STILL called their God (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; 49:33).

cards.question: Jesus says the Lord is not the God of the ___, but of the ___, for to Him all are alive.

cards.text: Some of the scribes answer, “Teacher, You have spoken well!” Wait. The SCRIBES? Friend, I almost dropped a whole tray of cookies.

cards.question: After all that, what do the people questioning Jesus do?

answers.text: They don't dare question Him any further
They bring Him an even harder question
They ask Him to show them a sign

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out that the authority is the governor rather than the high priest or a king. The blank therefore tests an unseen detail by luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about Jesus, "Me, friend?" and the sentence about packing a cookie box.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The earlier cards establish that the spies failed to trap Jesus, but they give no basis for reasoning out their reaction. "Amazed" and "silent" cannot be inferred any more reliably than being angry or laughing, so both blanks depend on guessing unseen wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the introduction of the Sadducees, "Friend, that's round two." and "DING DING."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Neither this question nor the earlier cards clearly state Luke 20:33's key premise that all seven brothers were married to the woman. Card 6 mentions the second and third marriages and then says only that all seven died, leaving out an important part of what makes the Sadducees' riddle work.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: Jesus' statement, "Notice that word, friend." and "THIS age."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "To show it" makes "it" point back to card 12's statement that the dead are raised. That antecedent is not supplied in the question itself.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 12 says that Moses demonstrates the resurrection but gives no clue about the burning object. The baker cannot reason out "bush" rather than "altar" or "mountain" from the earlier cards.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences: the scribes' response, "Wait.", "The SCRIBES?" and the sentence about dropping the cookies.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
